messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — after landing the kernel-selection tweak + new batching heuristic, we see a regression on PP/TP configs when activation checkpointing is enabled. KV cache enabled workloads look worse. Uploading short profile snapshot.

jonathan: Numbers? which config?

maria: batch=8, seq=2048, model=redwood-13B-serve, TP=2 PP=2, rematerialization=on (activation checkpointing), kv_cache=on. Throughput down ~9% and p99 latency +18% vs baseline (no remat).

sasha: Putting the nvprof snippet here — grabbed the hot-path times from the perf job:```
AllReduceKernel (v2): 12.4ms -> 28.1ms (remat on)
ForwardKern_X: 6.1ms
RecomputeForward: 5.9ms (extra)
CUDA memcpy/overlap: spiky
Total per-token compute+comm: 35ms -> 52ms
```

kyle: That allreduce jump smells like more frequent smaller communicatons rather than one fused op. Remat causes extra forward passes that interleave with reduces; do we have fusion disabled for the new kernel routing?

maria: Kernel routing change introduced a stricter packing heuristic for compute kernels (chooses narrow kernels to minimize memory), which reduced opportunities for allreduce fusion. With remat we now trigger an extra allreduce per remat block.

jonathan: So hypothesis: remat increases number of allreduces (N_remat_blocks * n_microbatches) -> more comm ops, smaller sizes -> poor BW utilization and less overlap with compute. Can we confirm #allreduce ops from trace?

sasha: I added NVTX markers and traced a single step. Trace shows 6 allreduces baseline -> 11 allreduces remat-on. Each is ~2x smaller in bytes and each has ~1.5x overhead. Overlap windows shrink because recompute kernels occupy the thread that would have overlapped late-stage allreduce.

kyle: Two quick mitigations to try: (1) change remat granularity to coarser blocks (reduce number of recomputes), (2) enable allreduce fusion in the runtime when it sees back-to-back small reductions. Also consider steering kernel selection to prefer slightly larger compute kernels that enable fusion.

maria: Agree. Also KV cache + generation causes irregular sequence lengths; when KV cache miss triggers extra recompute we get non-uniform microbatching which kills steady-state fusion. Could try prefetching KV shards to reduce misses.

benchbot: perf-job 1930001111-run1 finished — throughput -8.7% vs baseline, p99 +15%. Config: same as maria noted. Full artifacts: https://ci.internal/arch/1930001111-run1 (link). :bar_chart:

jonathan: Plan: I'll run a 3x sweep — remat_block_size in [2,4,8], kernel_routing=fuse_favoring|mem_favoring, enable_allreduce_fusion=true/false. Sasha add NVTX to all remat entry/exit. Kyle can you prototype a lightweight fusion pass that merges consecutive allreduces within X ms?

sasha: NVTX markers done in my branch, will push in 10m. Also adding a flamegraph export hook.

kyle: I'll spike the fusion pass. If we can merge small allreduces into fewer larger ones the bandwidth utilization should improve. Also will add a heuristic to avoid triggering fusion when remat introduces recompute overlap risk.

maria: If fusion helps, we should still gate behind policy per-cfg because some enterprise customers rely on strict mem tradeoffs. Also open to a runtime flag: remat-aware-fusion=true.

jonathan: One more idea: change batching heuristic to prefer slightly larger microbatches for TP/PP combos when remat is on — that amortizes the fixed allreduce overhead. I'll include that in the sweep.

sasha: Quick note: traces show a periodic spike in PCIe latency coincident with KV shard syncs. Those syncs line up with remat boundaries. Might be an IO scheduling interaction.

maria: Good catch. Sasha, can you annotate trace with KV-sync markers and we can see if moving KV sync slightly earlier/later reduces overlap with allreduce?

sasha: Yup will add.

kyle: For immediate triage — do a controlled run: remat off, kernel-routing new, kv_cache on vs remat on, kernel-routing old, kv_cache on. We need to isolate kernel-routing vs remat vs kv interplay.

maria: Agreed. Jonathan, can you kick off those runs and paste perf diffs here? I'll open an issue to track remediation steps and attach the PR links.

jonathan: Starting runs now. ETA ~45m. Will post summarized diffs when done.

maria: Thanks. If we find fusion fixes it we can ship a hotfix to the kernel selector and add remat-aware defaults. Otherwise we'll roll back the packing heuristic.

kyle: ping me when results in. If fusion helps I'll draft the opt-in PR and a perf test.

maria: Scheduling a 30m sync at 1600 to review results. @everyone please bring traces. :calendar:
